This Bodhisattva further transformed and enlightened ten trillion beings, causing them to dwell in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
After his life came to an end, he encountered two thousand billion Buddhas, all of whom were named Candrasūryapradīpa; within their teachings, he preached this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.

By these causes and conditions, he further encountered two thousand billion Buddhas, all equally named Cloud Sovereign Lamp King (*Meghasvaradīparāja*). Within the teachings of these Buddhas, because he upheld, recited, and read this sutra, and expounded it for the fourfold assembly, he attained this constant purity of the eye, as well as the purity of the faculties of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; thus, when preaching the Dharma among the fourfold assembly, his mind was free from fear.
“Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Constantly Regarded as Light made offerings to this many Buddhas, honoring, respecting, praising, and planting various roots of goodness. Thereafter, he again encountered thousands of myriads of koṭis of Buddhas, and likewise preached this sutra within the teachings of those Buddhas. Having accomplished such merit, he shall attain Buddhahood.”
“Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
What do you think?
Was the Bodhisattva Never Disparaging at that time anyone other than this person?”
I am that very person.
Had I not, in past lives, upheld, recited, and read this sutra, and had I not explained it to others, I would not have been able to quickly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Because I received, upheld, recited, and read this sutra under previous Buddhas, and explained it for others, I quickly attained Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
“Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

Because those four assemblies at that time—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—slandered me with thoughts of anger and contempt, for two hundred billion kalpas they shall never encounter a Buddha, hear the Dharma, or see the Sangha; and for a thousand kalpas they shall undergo great suffering and affliction in the Avīci Hell.”
Once these karmic retributions were exhausted, he again encountered the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging, who taught and transformed him toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Mahāsthāmaprāpta, what do you think?"
As for those in the fourfold assembly who at that time constantly disparaged this bodhisattva—could they have been anyone else?

They are none other than the five hundred bodhisattvas in this assembly, such as Bhadrapāla; the five hundred bhikṣus, such as Siṃhacandra; and the five hundred upāsakas, such as Niścitabuddhi—all of whom are non-retrogressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
You should know that this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* brings great benefit to all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and is able to lead them to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
Therefore, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, should constantly uphold, recite, explain, and transcribe this sutra.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"In the past there was a Buddha Named King of Majestic Sound;
His spiritual wisdom was immeasurable, And he led all beings— Gods, humans, dragons, and spirits— Who all made offerings to him together."
After this Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, when the Dharma was about to perish,
there was a bodhisattva named Sadāparibhūta.
At that time, the fourfold assembly was attached to the teachings.
The Bodhisattva Never Disparaging went to where they were and spoke to them, saying:
"I do not disparage you; as you all practice the Way, you shall all become Buddhas."
When the people heard this, they treated him with contempt, reviled, and abused him;
yet the Bodhisattva did not slight them and was able to endure it all.
Once his retribution for those offenses was exhausted, at the time of his death, he was able to hear this sutra, and his six sense faculties became pure.
By means of his supernormal powers, he increases his lifespan and further expounds this sutra extensively for all people.
All those who were attached to dharmas receive the bodhisattva’s instruction and transformation, achieving fulfillment and being established in the Buddha-way.
By preaching this sutra, one attains immeasurable merit; gradually perfecting all virtues, one swiftly achieves the Buddha-way.
At that time, the one named "Not Disparaging" was none other than myself.
At that time, among the fourfold assembly, those who were attached to the Dharma heard the words of the One Who Is Not Disparaging:
"You shall become a Buddha.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, they encountered countless Buddhas.
The assembly of five hundred bodhisattvas in this gathering, together with the fourfold assembly of laymen and laywomen of pure faith—
these are the ones who now listen to the Dharma before me.
In my previous lives, I exhorted these people to listen to and receive this sutra,
the supreme Dharma.
I revealed and taught it to others, causing them to abide in nirvana, so that they might uphold such a scripture in every lifetime.
For billions upon billions of kalpas, until they reach the inconceivable, one may finally hear this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
For billions upon billions of kalpas, until they reach the inconceivable, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, preach this sūtra at such times.
Therefore, practitioners, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, upon hearing such a sūtra as this, should not give rise to doubt or confusion.
You should with a single mind widely expound this sūtra; thus you shall encounter Buddhas in every lifetime and swiftly attain the path of Buddhahood.

Chapter 21: The Tathāgata’s Supernatural Powers *The Lotus Sutra, Chapter Twenty-one: The Tathāgata’s Supernatural Powers* At that time, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the atoms in a thousand worlds, who had emerged from the earth, all stood before the Buddha with single-minded palms joined. Gazing up at the Honored One’s countenance, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"After the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, wherever the emanations of the World-Honored One reside and wherever he has attained extinction, we shall extensively proclaim this sutra. Why is this? "
"We ourselves also wish to obtain this truly pure Great Dharma, to receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, transcribe, and make offerings to it.

At that time, the World-Honored One, before the assembly of Mañjuśrī and countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had long resided in the Sahā world, as well as the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all others, manifested great supernatural power: he extended his broad and long tongue until it reached the Brahma-world, and from every pore he emitted immeasurable and innumerable rays of light of various colors, which completely illuminated the worlds of the ten directions.
The Buddhas beneath the various jewel trees on their lion thrones did likewise, extending their broad and long tongues and emitting immeasurable light.
When Śākyamuni Buddha and the Buddhas beneath the jewel trees manifested this supernatural power, it continued for a full hundred thousand years, after which they withdrew their tongue-marks.
At that moment, they coughed and simultaneously snapped their fingers; these two sounds reached all the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, and the earth in each shook in six ways.

The sentient beings therein—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth—by the supernatural power of the Buddha, all beheld these Buddhas beneath immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of jewel trees and upon lion thrones in this Sahā world;
they also saw Śākyamuni Buddha together with the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna within the jeweled stupa, seated upon a lion throne;
and they further saw immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the fourfold assembly reverently surrounding Śākyamuni Buddha.
Having seen this, they were all filled with great joy, having attained what they had never experienced before.
Immediately, the devas in the midst of the void raised their voices and proclaimed:

"Beyond these immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of asaṃkhyeya worlds, there is a land named Sahā; therein dwells a Buddha named Śākyamuni, who is now preaching for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas a Mahāyāna sūtra titled the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, the Dharma taught to bodhisattvas, which is protected by the Buddhas."
"You all should rejoice with a profound heart, and you should also pay homage and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha.
When those sentient beings heard the voice from the sky, they joined their palms toward the Sahā world and spoke these words:
"Namo Śākyamuni Buddha!"
"Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha!

With various flowers, incense, necklaces, banners, canopies, as well as all manner of ornaments for the body and precious, wonderful objects, they all together scattered them from afar toward the Sahā world.
The various objects scattered [as offerings] came from the ten directions like gathering clouds; they transformed into a jeweled canopy that completely covered all the Buddhas present there.
At that time, the worlds of the ten directions became unobstructed and interconnected, as if they were a single Buddha-field.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly of bodhisattvas, including Śūraṅgama and the others:

"The spiritual power of the Buddhas is thus—immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Even if I were to use this spiritual power to describe the merits of this sutra for the sake of entrustment throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I would still not be able to exhaust them."

To summarize: all the dharmas possessed by the Tathāgata, all the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata, all the secret and essential treasuries of the Tathāgata, and all the most profound matters of the Tathāgata are proclaimed and revealed within this sutra.
Therefore, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, you should with single-minded devotion uphold, read, recite, explain, transcribe, and practice according to the teaching.

In whatever land this [sūtra] may be upheld, recited, explained, written down, or practiced according to its teaching; wherever the scroll of this sūtra may reside—whether in a garden, a grove, beneath a tree, in a monastery, in a layperson’s house, in a hall, or in a mountain valley or wilderness—in all such places one should erect a stūpa and make offerings.

Why is this so? You should know that this very place is the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa); it is here that all Buddhas attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), it is here that all Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma, and it is here that all Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke these verses: "The Buddhas, the saviors of the world, Abiding in great supernormal powers,
For the sake of gladdening sentient beings, Manifest immeasurable spiritual powers."
The mark of his tongue reaches the Brahma-heaven; from his body he emits countless rays of light.
For those who seek the Buddha-way, he manifests this rare and marvelous event.
The sound of the Buddhas’ clearing their throats, as well as the sound of their snapping fingers—
The sounds were heard throughout the lands of the ten directions, and the earth shook in six ways.
Because one is able to uphold this sutra after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
all Buddhas rejoice and manifest immeasurable supernatural powers.
Because I entrust this sutra to you, even if one were to praise and extol those who receive and uphold it for immeasurable eons,
one could still never fully exhaust the description of that person’s merit; it is boundless and without end.
Just as the empty space of the ten directions, Its boundaries cannot be found; so too,
those who can uphold this sutra Have already seen me,
And have also seen the Buddha Prabhūtaratna, As well as all his emanated bodies.
Furthermore, seeing me today teaching and transforming all bodhisattvas,
those who are able to uphold this sutra will cause me, my manifested bodies,
and the Buddha Prabhūtaratna who has entered parinirvāṇa— all to rejoice.
The Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, as well as those of the past and future—
I see them all and make offerings to them, causing them all to attain joy.
The secret and essential Dharma attained by the Buddhas when seated at the site of enlightenment—
Those who are able to uphold this sutra will, before long, likewise attain it.
Those who are able to uphold this sutra will, regarding the meaning of all dharmas,
their names, and their terminology, delight in explaining them without end.
Just as the wind moves through space without any obstruction, so too,
after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, one who understands the sūtras spoken by the Buddha—
their causes, conditions, and sequence— will explain them according to their meaning and in accordance with reality.
Just as the light of the sun and moon can dispel all darkness,
so too this person, walking through the world, can extinguish the gloom of sentient beings;
they instruct immeasurable bodhisattvas, causing them ultimately to abide in the One Vehicle.
Therefore, those who possess wisdom, having heard these benefits of merit,
should uphold this sutra after my parinirvāṇa;
such persons will have no doubt whatsoever regarding the Buddha-way.

**Chapter 22: Entrustment** *The Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma, Chapter Twenty-Two: Entrustment* At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha rose from his Dharma-seat and manifested great supernormal powers. With his right hand, he stroked the heads of immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and spoke these words:
"For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have cultivated this Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, which is so difficult to attain; I now entrust it to you."
"You all should single-mindedly propagate this Dharma and cause it to increase and flourish extensively.
Having thus placed his hand upon the crowns of the heads of these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas three times, he spoke these words:
"For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have cultivated this rare Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; I now entrust it to you."
"You all should receive, uphold, read, recite, and widely proclaim this Dharma, so that all sentient beings may universally hear and know it.

Why is this? The Tathāgata possesses great compassion, is free from all stinginess and parsimony, and has no fear; he is able to bestow upon sentient beings the Buddha’s wisdom, the Tathāgata’s wisdom, and the self-arisen wisdom. The Tathāgata is the great benefactor of all sentient beings."
You all should likewise follow and study the Dharma of the Tathāgata, and do not give rise to stinginess or parsimony.

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who believe in the wisdom of the Tathāgata, you should expound this Lotus Sūtra for them so that they may hear and know it, in order to enable those people to attain the Buddha-wisdom.
If there are sentient beings who do not believe and accept [this teaching], you should instruct, benefit, and gladden them by pointing toward other profound dharmas of the Tathāgata.
If you are able to act in this way, you will have repaid the kindness of all Buddhas.

At that time, when the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas had heard this teaching of the Buddha, great joy filled their entire bodies; they increased their reverence even further, bowing with bent bodies and lowered heads, and joining their palms toward the Buddha, they spoke in unison:
“As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall carry it out in full.”
"So be it, World-Honored One!
We pray that you have no concern.
Thus did the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, repeating this three times, all speak with one voice:
“As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall carry it out in full.
So be it, World-Honored One!
We pray that you have no further concern.”
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha commanded the various emanated Buddhas who had come from the ten directions to each return to their own lands, saying:
"May the Buddhas each go wherever they find rest, and let the stupa of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna return to its former state."

When these words were spoken, the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions who had manifested as emanations and were seated upon lion thrones beneath jeweled trees, as well as the Buddha Prabhūtaratna, the boundless assembly of asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas such as Urdhvaṅgama, the fourfold assembly of śrāvakas such as Śāriputra, and all the world’s devas, humans, and asuras, having heard what the Buddha had said, were all filled with great joy.

Chapter Twenty-Three: The Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja The Lotus Sutra, Chapter Twenty-Three: The Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja At that time, the Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"How does the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja roam through the Sahā world?
World-Honored One!
How many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of difficult and painful practices has this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja performed?"
"Excellent, World-Honored One!
We pray that you will briefly explain this.

Upon hearing this, the devas, nāgas, spirits, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, as well as the bodhisattvas who had come from other lands and the assembly of śrāvakas here, were all filled with joy.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña:

"In the distant past, immeasurable kalpas ago, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there was a Buddha named Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat."

That Buddha had eight billion great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and a great assembly of voice-hearers as numerous as the sands of seventy-two Ganges Rivers; the Buddha’s lifespan was forty-two thousand kalpas, and the lifespans of the bodhisattvas were equal to his.
In that land there are no women, nor are there hells, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, or any such calamities;

the ground is as level as the palm of a hand, composed of lapis lazuli, adorned with jeweled trees, and covered above by jeweled canopies from which hang jeweled flower banners. Jeweled vases and incense burners are distributed throughout the realm, and there are pedestals made of the seven treasures—one pedestal for each tree—with each tree situated at a distance of one arrow-shot from its pedestal.
Beneath all these jewel trees sit bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
Upon each of the jewel terraces, ten billion devas perform celestial music and sing praises of the Buddha as an act of offering.
At that time, that Buddha was preaching the Lotus Sūtra for the sake of the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, as well as for the assembly of bodhisattvas and the multitude of śrāvakas.

"This Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana delighted in practicing asceticism; within the Dharma of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, he practiced walking meditation with diligence and sought Buddhahood with a single mind. After twelve thousand years had passed, he attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms."
Having attained this samādhi, his heart was filled with great joy, and he immediately thought:

"That I have attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Bodies is entirely due to the power of hearing the Lotus Sūtra; I shall now make offerings to the Buddha Sun Moon Pure Bright Virtue and to the Lotus Sūtra."

Immediately he entered this samādhi, and from the midst of space there rained down *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, and finely ground black sandalwood, filling the void and descending like clouds. Furthermore, there rained down the fragrance of *gośīrṣa* sandalwood—six *zhu* of this incense being worth as much as the entire Sahā world—to make offerings to the Buddha.
Having made this offering, he arose from samādhi and thought to himself:
"Although I have made offerings to the Buddha through supernatural powers, it is not as good as making an offering with my own body."

He then consumed various incenses—sandalwood, olibanum, turushka, parpaka, aloeswood, and resin—and drank the fragrant oils of the *campaka* and other flowers. After twelve hundred years had passed, he anointed his body with fragrant oil and, before the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, wrapped himself in celestial precious robes. He poured fragrant oils over himself and, through the power of his supernatural vows, caused his own body to manifest, its radiance illuminating worlds as numerous as the sands of eighty billion Ganges Rivers.
Therein, all the Buddhas simultaneously praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
This is true diligence; this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata.

It cannot be equaled by offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense, ointment incense, celestial silks, banners, canopies, or even the sandalwood from the other side of the sea, nor by such various items as these.
Even the giving away of kingdoms, cities, wives, and children does not approach it.
“Good sons!
This is called the foremost gift; it is the most honored and supreme among all gifts, for it is the offering of the Dharma to all Tathāgatas.
Having spoken these words, they each became silent.
His body burned for twelve hundred years, and only after this period had passed was his body finally consumed.

After the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana had performed such a Dharma-offering, at the end of his life, he was reborn in the land of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, where he suddenly manifested by transformation, sitting cross-legged in the house of King Viśuddhaśrī.
He then spoke these verses for his father:
“Great King, you should now know: As I was walking there, I immediately attained the samādhi That manifests all bodies.”
"Exerting great diligence, he sacrificed his beloved body to make offerings to the World-Honored One, seeking unsurpassed wisdom.
Having spoken this verse, he addressed his father, saying:
"The Buddha Sun-Moon Pure Bright Virtue still exists in the present.

Having previously made offerings to that Buddha, I attained the dhāraṇī for understanding the languages of all sentient beings, and further heard eight hundred thousand myriads of koṭis of nayutas of *khangara*, *bimbara*, and *akṣobhya* verses of this Lotus Sutra."
"Great King!
I shall now return to make offerings to this Buddha.

Having spoken thus, he immediately sat upon a terrace of the seven precious gems and ascended into the void to a height of seven *tāla* trees. Arriving at the place where the Buddha was, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, joined his ten fingers and toes in reverence, and praised the Buddha with these verses:
“Your countenance is most wondrous and sublime, Your radiance illuminates the ten directions.
I have previously made offerings to you, And now I come once more to behold you in person.”
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana had spoken these verses, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
The World-Honored One still remains in the world."
At that time, the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa addressed the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana: "Good son!
The time for my parinirvāṇa has arrived; the moment of my final extinction is at hand. You should prepare a seat, for I shall enter parinirvāṇa this very night."
He further commanded the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana: "Good son!

I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you and to all the bodhisattvas and great śrāvakas, as well as the dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. I also entrust to you this trichiliocosm of the seven-jeweled world, including its jeweled trees, jeweled terraces, and the attendant devas."
"After my parinirvāṇa, all my relics are also entrusted to you; you should cause them to be widely distributed and extensively honored, and you should erect several thousand stūpas."
After the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa had thus instructed the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, he entered parinirvāṇa during the latter part of the night.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, seeing the Buddha’s passing, was filled with grief and distress; longing for the Buddha, he used *candana* sandalwood from this side of the sea to construct a pyre and cremated the Buddha’s body as an offering.

After the fire had been extinguished, they collected the śarīra and fashioned eighty-four thousand precious jars, with which they erected eighty-four thousand stupas. These were three worlds in height, adorned with ornate spires, draped with banners and canopies, and hung with many jeweled bells.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana again thought to himself:
"Although I have made these offerings, my mind is still not satisfied; I shall now further offer worship to the relics."
He then addressed the assembly of all bodhisattvas, great disciples, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others:
“You should all focus your minds with single-mindedness; I am now making offerings to the relics of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī.”

Having spoken these words, he immediately before eighty-four thousand stupas burned his arm—adorned with a hundred merits—for seventy-two thousand years as an act of offering. He caused countless seekers of the śrāvaka vehicle and immeasurable asaṃkhyeya people to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and enabled them all to abide in the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Bodies.
At that time, the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, and others, seeing that he was without arms, were filled with grief and sorrow, and spoke these words:
"This Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana is our teacher and the one who instructs us; yet now he has burned his arms, and his body is no longer complete."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana made this vow before the great assembly:
"I shall sacrifice both my arms; I must surely attain the golden body of a Buddha. If this is true and not false, let my two arms be restored as they were before."
Having made this vow, [the earth] naturally returned to its original state, brought about by the profound depth of the Bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom.
At that moment, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down precious flowers; all humans and devas attained what they had never experienced before.
The Buddha said to the Bodhisattva Puṣpākara: "What do you think?
Is the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana anyone other than this person?"
This is none other than the present Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
The number of times he has sacrificed his body as an act of giving is thus immeasurable—hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions, billions, and nayutas of times.
"Sukhāvatīrāja! [Listen well!]"

If there are those who resolve their minds to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and are able to burn a finger, or even a single toe, as an offering to a Buddha-stūpa, this surpasses the merit of one who offers kingdoms, cities, wives, children, and the mountains, forests, rivers, lakes, and all manner of rare treasures throughout the three-thousandfold world system. Furthermore, if someone were to fill the three-thousandfold world system with the seven treasures and offer them to the Buddhas, as well as to great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats, the merit obtained by that person would not equal the merit of one who upholds even a single four-line verse of this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*; the latter’s blessings are the greatest.
“Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā!
Just as among all streams, currents, and great rivers, the ocean is foremost;
so too is this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, for among all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, it is the most profound and vast.”

Furthermore, just as among all mountains—the Earth Mountains, the Black Mountains, the Lesser Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, and the Ten Treasure Mountains—Mount Sumeru is the foremost;
so too is this Lotus Sutra, which is the most supreme among all sutras.
Furthermore, just as among all the stars the Moon Deity is the foremost, so too is this Lotus Sūtra;
it is the most illuminating among the hundreds of thousands of millions of various sūtras and teachings.
Furthermore, just as the Sun Deva is able to dispel all darkness, so too is this sutra, for it can shatter the darkness of all unwholesome states.
Moreover, just as among all minor kings, the Wheel-Turning Sage King is the foremost; so it is with this sutra.
This sutra is likewise thus; among all sutras, it is the most honored.
Furthermore, just as Śakra is the king among the Thirty-three Gods, so too is this sutra the king among all sutras.
Furthermore, just as Mahābrahmā is the father of all sentient beings,
so too is this sutra the father of all worthy and noble ones— those in training (*śaikṣa*), those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), and those who have resolved to attain the bodhisattva mind.
Furthermore, just as among all ordinary persons, the *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, *arhat*, and *pratyekabuddha* are the foremost;
so too is this sutra: among all the sūtras and dharmas spoken by all Tathāgatas, or by bodhisattvas, or by śrāvakas, it is the most supreme.
One who is able to receive and uphold this sutra is likewise so; among all sentient beings, they are also the foremost.
Among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the bodhisattva is the foremost;
this sutra is also like this, being the most supreme among all the dharmas of the various sutras.
"Just as the Buddha is the king of all dharmas,
so too is this sutra the king among all sutras.
O Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!

This sutra can save all sentient beings; this sutra can cause all sentient beings to be free from all suffering and affliction; this sutra can greatly benefit all sentient beings, fulfilling their aspirations.
It is like a pond of cool water that can satisfy all who are parched with thirst;

it is like fire for one who is cold, like clothing for one who is naked, like a master for a merchant, like a mother for a child, like a boat for one crossing over, like a physician for the sick, like a lamp in the darkness, like treasure for the poor, like a king for his subjects, like the ocean for a trader, and like a torch that dispels the dark.
This Lotus Sūtra is also like this: it can cause sentient beings to leave behind all suffering and all ailments, and it can untie all the bonds of birth and death.

If a person hears this Lotus Sūtra, whether they write it themselves or cause others to write it, the merit they obtain is such that even if one were to measure its extent with the wisdom of a Buddha, its limit could not be reached.

If one writes out this sutra scroll and makes offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense, ointment incense, banners, canopies, and robes, as well as various kinds of lamps—butter lamps, oil lamps, lamps of various fragrant oils, *campaka* oil lamps, *sumanā* oil lamps, *pāṭala* oil lamps, *vārṣika* oil lamps, and *navamālikā* oil lamps—the merit obtained will likewise be immeasurable.
“Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā!
If there are those who hear this ‘Chapter on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,’ they shall also attain immeasurable and boundless merit.

If there are women who hear this ‘Chapter on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja’ and are able to receive and uphold it, they will exhaust their female bodies and shall never again assume them.”

If, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, during the final five hundred years, there should be women who hear this sutra and practice according to its teachings, at the end of their lives they shall immediately go to the World of Peace and Bliss, the dwelling place surrounded by Amitābha Buddha and the great assembly of bodhisattvas.

They shall be born within lotus flowers upon jeweled thrones; they shall no longer be afflicted by desire, nor afflicted by anger or ignorance, nor afflicted by the defilements of pride, jealousy, and other impurities. They shall attain the supernatural powers of a bodhisattva and the realization of the non-arising of all phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).

Having attained this patience, their faculty of the eye becomes pure; with this purified faculty of the eye, they behold seven million two thousand billion nayutas of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
At that time, all the Buddhas praised him from afar, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"

If you are able, within the Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha, to receive, uphold, read, recite, and contemplate this sutra, and to explain it for others, the merit you obtain will be immeasurable and boundless; fire cannot burn it, nor can water wash it away. As for your merit, even if a thousand Buddhas were to speak of it together, they could not exhaust it.
You have now been able to defeat the various demonic marauders and destroy the army of birth and death; all other enemies have been utterly crushed.
Son of good family!

Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, through their supernormal powers, protect you together. Among all the devas and humans in every world, there is no one like you, except for the Tathāgata. As for all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and even bodhisattvas, none possess wisdom or meditative concentration equal to yours.
"Rājanvṛkṣapūṣpa! This Bodhisattva has accomplished such power of merit and wisdom.

If there is anyone who, upon hearing this 'Chapter on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,' can rejoice in it and praise it as excellent, that person in their present life will constantly have the fragrance of blue lotuses issue from their mouth, and the fragrance of ox-head sandalwood will constantly issue from the pores of their body; the merit they obtain shall be as described above."
Therefore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!
I entrust this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva" to you.

After my parinirvāṇa, during the final five hundred years, you must propagate it widely throughout Jambudvīpa so that it does not come to an end, lest evil Māras, their followers, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others find an opportunity to cause harm.
“Ratnakusuma! You should protect this sutra by means of your supernormal powers. Why is this?
This sutra serves as an excellent medicine for the illnesses of the people of Jambudvīpa.
If anyone who is ill hears this sutra, their illness will be immediately extinguished, and they shall neither grow old nor die.
Rājanvatsapuṣpa!
If you see anyone who upholds this sutra, you should take blue lotuses filled with powdered incense and scatter them over that person.
Having scattered them, you should form this thought:

"This person will, before long, surely take grass and sit at the site of enlightenment; he shall destroy the armies of Māra, blow the conch of the Dharma, and beat the great drum of the Dharma, delivering all sentient beings from the ocean of old age, sickness, and death."
"Therefore, those who seek the Buddha-way, upon seeing anyone who receives and upholds this sutra, should give rise to a heart of reverence such as this.
When this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva" was being spoken, eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas attained the dhāraṇī for understanding the languages of all sentient beings.
From within the jeweled stupa, the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna praised the Bodhisattva Rājādhiṣṭhānavaśavartin, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Rājādhiṣṭhānavaśavartin!
You have accomplished inconceivable merit that you are able to ask Śākyamuni Buddha about such matters as these, thereby benefiting immeasurable sentient beings.
The Lotus Sutra, Scroll Six; The Lotus Sutra, Scroll Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Kucha during the Later Qin Dynasty.
Translated by Kumārajīva by Imperial Decree.

Chapter Twenty-Four: The Chapter on Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha emitted the radiance from the *uṣṇīṣa*—the mark of a Great Man—and emitted the radiance from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, which shone throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the eastern direction.

Beyond this number, there is a world named Pure Light Adornment. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One. He is surrounded by and reverently attended by an immeasurable and boundless assembly of bodhisattvas as he preaches the Dharma; the radiance from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of Śākyamuni Buddha shines throughout that entire land.
At that time, in the land of Universal Pure Light Adornment, there was a bodhisattva named Gadgadasvara,
who had long since planted the roots of manifold virtues and had served and attended upon immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddhas,
thereby fully accomplishing profound wisdom and attaining the Samādhi of the Wondrous Banner and the Lotus Samādhi.
...the Samādhi of Pure Virtue, the Samādhi of the Play of the Constellations, the Samādhi of the Objectless, the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom,
the Samādhi of Understanding the Languages of All Sentient Beings, the Samādhi of Accumulating All Merit, the Samādhi of Purity,
the Samādhi of the Play of Supernatural Powers, the Samādhi of the Torch of Wisdom, and the Samādhi of the Adorned King.
The Samādhi, the Samādhi of Pure Radiance, the Samādhi of the Pure Treasury, the Unshared Samādhi,
and the Sun-Turning Samādhi— he attained hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of such great samādhis, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
The light of Śākyamuni Buddha illuminated his body, and he addressed the Buddha Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom, saying:
"World-Honored One!

I shall go to the Sahā world to pay homage to, draw near to, and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha; and to see the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, the Bodhisattva Viśiṣṭadatta, the Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, the Bodhisattva Lakṣaṇaprabha, and the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata."
At that time, the Buddha Śubhavyūhapadmavuṣitacintāmaṇicakravartin addressed the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara:
"Do not disparage that land, nor give rise to thoughts of it being inferior.
Good son!..."

That Sahā world is uneven, with high and low ground; it is filled with mountains of earth and stone and abounds in filth and impurity. The Buddha’s body is short and small, and the forms of the assembly of bodhisattvas are likewise small.

Your body is forty-two thousand yojanas in height, while my body is six million eight hundred thousand yojanas. Your body is foremost in its beauty, possessing hundreds of thousands of millions of blessings, with a radiance that is exceptionally sublime; therefore, go there and do not disparage that land—do not conceive thoughts of inferiority toward the Buddha, the bodhisattvas, or the buddha-field.
The Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara addressed his Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
That I now journey to the Sahā world is entirely through the power of the Tathāgata, the playful mastery of the Tathāgata’s supernormal powers, and the adornment of the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom."

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara, without rising from his seat and without his body moving, entered a samādhi. By the power of that samādhi, not far from the Dharma-seat on Vulture Peak Mountain, he manifested eighty-four thousand lotus flowers made of various jewels, with stems of Jāmbūnada gold, leaves of white silver, filaments of diamond, and pericarps of kiṃśuka gems.
At that time, the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, seeing these lotus flowers, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
By what causes and conditions has this auspicious omen first appeared?"
There were several tens of millions of lotus flowers, with stems of Jāmbūnada gold, petals of white silver, filaments of diamond, and pericarps made of kiṃśuka gems.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī:

“This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara wishes to come from the land of the Buddha Śubhavyūharāja, surrounded by eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas, to this Sahā world in order to make offerings to, attend upon, and prostrate before me, and also to make offerings to and listen to the Lotus Sūtra.”
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What roots of goodness has this bodhisattva planted?”
What merit has been cultivated to enable such great supernormal powers?
What samādhi has been practiced?

We pray that you will tell us the name of this samādhi; we also wish to diligently practice it, for by practicing this samādhi, we shall be able to see the physical appearance, stature, and dignified deportment of this bodhisattva.
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, by means of your supernatural powers, will cause that bodhisattva to come so that I may behold him.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
“This Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, who entered parinirvāṇa long ago, shall now manifest his form for your sake.”
Then the Buddha Prabhūtaratna addressed that bodhisattva:
"Good son, come! The Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī wishes to see you."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara vanished from that land and set out together with eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas.
As they passed through various lands, the earth shook in six ways, and everywhere there fell rain from the seven precious jewels in the form of lotus flowers;
hundreds of thousands of celestial musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck.

The eyes of this bodhisattva are like the petals of a vast blue lotus; even if a hundred thousand million moons were brought together, his countenance would be more upright and handsome than that. His body is of true golden color, adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of merits; his majestic virtue is blazing and his radiance shines forth, as he is fully endowed with all the marks, possessing a body as firm and solid as Nārāyaṇa.

Entering a pavilion made of the seven treasures, they ascended into the void to a height of seven *tāla* trees above the ground; surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas who paid them respectful homage, they came to this Sahā world, to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.

Having arrived, he descended from the seven-jeweled terrace and, taking a necklace worth hundreds of thousands, went to where Śākyamuni Buddha was. He prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, presented the necklace, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha Śubhavyūharājasaṃkusumitābhijña inquires after the World-Honored One: Are you free from illness and affliction? Is your daily life light and easy? Do you dwell in peace and happiness?
Are the four great elements in harmony?
"Are worldly affairs bearable?
Are sentient beings easy to deliver?
Do they not have excessive greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, stinginess, or pride?"
"Is there no one who is unfilial toward their parents, disrespectful toward śramaṇas, possessed of wrong views, with an unwholesome mind, or who does not restrain the five sensory faculties?
World-Honored One!
Are sentient beings able to subdue all māras and enemies?"
Has the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, who entered parinirvāṇa long ago, come from within his stupa made of the seven treasures to listen to the Dharma?
Furthermore, inquire after the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna’s well-being: whether he is at ease, free from affliction, and able to endure remaining for a long time.
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to see the body of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna; I only pray that the World-Honored One will show it to me so that I may see it.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke to the Buddha Prabhūtaratna:
"This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara wishes to meet you.
At that time, the Buddha Prabhūtaratna addressed Gadgadasvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"It is because you were able to make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, listen to the Lotus Sutra, and behold Mañjuśrī and the others that you have come here.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Padmaśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"What roots of goodness did this Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara plant, and what merits did he cultivate, that he possesses such supernatural power?
The Buddha told Flower Virtue Bodhisattva:

"In the past, there was a Buddha named Cloud Thunder Sound King (*Meghadundubhisvararāja*), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. His land was named Manifesting All Worlds (*Sarvalokadarśana*), and his eon was named Joyful to Behold (*Priyadarśana*). For twelve thousand years, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara made offerings to the Buddha Cloud Thunder Sound King with one hundred thousand kinds of musical instruments and presented him with eighty-four thousand bowls made of the seven precious gems."
By reason of these causes and conditions and their karmic retribution, you have now been born in the land of the Buddha Śubhavyūhapadmottarajñānin, and thus possess such supernormal powers.
Flower Virtue! What do you think?

At that time, at the place of the Buddha King of Cloud-Thunder Sound, was the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara—who offered music as an act of worship and presented precious vessels—anyone other than this person?
"This is none other than the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara!
Flower Virtue,

this Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara has already made offerings to and drawn near to immeasurable Buddhas, long planting the roots of virtue, and has further encountered hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."
“Guṇarati! You see only that the body of the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara is here;
yet this Bodhisattva manifests various bodies, everywhere preaching this sutra for the sake of all sentient beings—sometimes manifesting as the body of Brahmā.”
Sometimes manifesting in the body of Śakra, sometimes manifesting in the body of Īśvara,
sometimes manifesting in the body of Maheśvara, sometimes manifesting in the body of a celestial general, sometimes manifesting in the body of Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Heavenly Kings,
sometimes manifesting in the body of a universal monarch (cakravartin), sometimes manifesting in the bodies of various minor kings, or sometimes manifesting in the body of a householder; or...
They manifest in the form of laypeople, or in the form of ministers and officials, or in the form of brahmins;
they manifest in the form of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās;
or they manifest in the form of elder laywomen, or in the form of the wives of ministers and officials, or in the form of brahmin women.
In the form of a woman, or manifesting in the form of a boy or a girl, or manifesting in the forms of devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, they preach this sūtra.

He is able to rescue and deliver all those in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, as well as those in various places of suffering; even within the royal harem, he transforms into a female body to preach this sutra.
“Śāradvatīputra!

This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara, who is able to protect all sentient beings in the Sahā world, manifests such various transformations and appearances here in this Sahā land to preach this sutra for the sake of all sentient beings; yet, he suffers no diminution in his supernatural powers, transformations, or wisdom.”
This bodhisattva, with various forms of wisdom, illuminates the Sahā world, causing all sentient beings therein to each attain what they need to know;
it is likewise so throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions.
If there are those who are to be liberated by means of the form of a śrāvaka, he manifests the form of a śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma for them;
if there are those who are to be liberated by means of the form of a pratyekabuddha, he manifests the form of a pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
if there are those who are to be liberated by means of the form of a bodhisattva, he manifests the form of a bodhisattva and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who are to be liberated by the form of a Buddha, he manifests the form of a Buddha and preaches the Dharma for them.
In such various ways, he manifests forms according to what is appropriate for each being to be liberated; even for those who are to be liberated through parinirvāṇa, he manifests parinirvāṇa.
“Flower Virtue!
Such are the deeds of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, who has accomplished the power of great supernormal abilities and wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Flower Virtue addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara has deeply planted roots of goodness.
World-Honored One!”
"In what samādhi does this bodhisattva abide, such that he is able to manifest transformations everywhere in this manner to deliver and liberate sentient beings?
The Buddha told Flower Virtue Bodhisattva:
"Good son!..."
The name of that samādhi is "Manifesting All Physical Bodies"; dwelling within this samādhi, the Bodhisattva Wonderful Sound is able to benefit immeasurable sentient beings in such a manner.

When this "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara" was being preached, the eighty-four thousand people who had come together with the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara all attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms;
likewise, immeasurable bodhisattvas in this Sahā world also attained this samādhi and dhāraṇīs.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara had made offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha, he returned to his own land; as he passed through the various countries, the earth shook in six ways, precious lotus flowers rained down, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kinds of musical instruments played.
Having arrived in his own land, surrounded by eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas, he went to the presence of the Buddha Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
I have come to the Sahā world to benefit sentient beings; there I have seen Śākyamuni Buddha and the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha, where I paid homage and made offerings.

Furthermore, I have seen the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, as well as the Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja, Vīryadattabalaprāpta, and Sūradatta, and I have also enabled these eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas to attain the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms.

When this chapter on the coming and going of the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara was being preached, forty-two thousand devaputras attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), and the Bodhisattva Puṣpadatta attained the Lotus Samādhi (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi).

The Universal Gate Chapter of the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty; prose section translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta of North India during the Sui Dynasty; Verse Section 25. The Universal Gate Chapter of the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Twenty-fifth Chapter of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him thus:
"World-Honored One!..."
"For what reasons and conditions is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara named 'Avalokiteśvara'?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati: "Good son!"

If there are immeasurable hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, or billions of sentient beings undergoing various sufferings and afflictions, and they hear of this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and single-mindedly invoke his name, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will immediately behold their voices, and they shall all attain liberation.
If there are those who hold the name of this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, even if they enter a great fire, the fire will not burn them, due to the majestic spiritual power of this Bodhisattva.
If one is being swept away by a great flood, by invoking his name, one will immediately reach shallow ground.

Suppose there are hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of sentient beings who, seeking treasures such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musāragalva, agate, coral, amber, and pearls, enter the great ocean.

Even if a black wind should blow their ship and cast it adrift into the land of the rākṣasa demons, if among them there is even a single person who calls upon the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, all those people shall be liberated from the peril of the rākṣasas.
For these reasons, he is named Avalokiteśvara.

Furthermore, if there is anyone who is about to be harmed and calls upon the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the swords and staves held by their assailants will immediately break into pieces, and they shall obtain liberation.

If yakṣas and rākṣasas were to fill the trichiliocosm, intending to come and harass people, yet hear someone invoking the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, these evil spirits would not even dare to look upon them with an evil eye, let alone inflict harm.

Furthermore, if there should be a person—whether guilty or innocent—who is bound and fettered in body by cangues, shackles, stocks, or manacles, and who invokes the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, all these bonds shall be broken and destroyed, and they shall immediately attain liberation.

Suppose that throughout a trichiliocosm there were bandits filling every corner, and a merchant leader, leading a caravan of merchants and carrying precious treasures, was traveling along a perilous road.
One among them made this proclamation:
"O sons of good family!
Do not be afraid!"
"You all should single-mindedly invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
This Bodhisattva is able to bestow fearlessness upon sentient beings.
If you invoke his name, you shall attain liberation from these hostile robbers."
Upon hearing this, the merchants all raised their voices together, saying:
"Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
By invoking his name, they immediately attained liberation.
"Akṣayamati! Such is the majestic and sublime power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.

If there are sentient beings who abound in lustful desires, by constantly mindfuly recollecting and reverently honoring the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, they shall immediately become free from desire."
If one has much anger, by constantly recollecting and reverently honoring Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one will immediately become free from anger.
If one has much ignorance, by constantly recollecting and reverently honoring Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one will immediately become free from ignorance.
"Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such great and majestic spiritual powers, bringing benefit to many.
For this reason, sentient beings should always keep him in mind."
If there is a woman who desires to have a son, by bowing in worship and making offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, she shall give birth to a son endowed with merit and wisdom;
if she desires to have a daughter, she shall give birth to a daughter who is upright and possesses auspicious marks.
Having planted roots of virtue in past lives, he is loved and respected by all people.
"Aksayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such power as this."
If there are sentient beings who pay homage and prostrate to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, their merit shall not be in vain.
For this reason, all sentient beings should uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

“Akṣayamati! Suppose there were someone who received and upheld the names of as many bodhisattvas as there are grains of sand in sixty-two billion Ganges Rivers, and furthermore, throughout their entire life, provided them with offerings of food and drink, clothing, bedding, and medicine.
"What do you think?
Would the merit of these good sons and good daughters be great? Ajita said:
“Very many, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said,
“If there are people who receive and uphold the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, even for a single moment bowing and making offerings to him.”
The merit of these two persons is exactly equal and without distinction; it cannot be exhausted even in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas. Ajita!
By upholding the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one obtains such benefits of immeasurable and boundless merit.
The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara travel through this Sahā world?”
"How does he preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings?
What is the nature of his power of skillful means?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati:

“Good son! If there are sentient beings in any land who are to be liberated by means of the Buddha-body, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva immediately manifests in the form of a Buddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
if they are to be liberated by means of the Pratyekabuddha-body, he immediately manifests in the form of a Pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them.”
To those who are to be liberated through the form of a śrāvaka, he manifests in the body of a śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who are to be liberated through the body of a Brahmā king, he manifests in the body of a Brahmā king and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who are to be liberated through the body of Śakra, he manifests in the body of Śakra and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be liberated through the form of Īśvara, he manifests the body of Īśvara and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who should be liberated through the body of Maheśvara, he manifests the body of Maheśvara and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who should be liberated through the body of a celestial general, he manifests the body of a celestial general and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who are to be saved by the form of Vaiśravaṇa, he manifests the body of Vaiśravaṇa and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who are to be saved by the form of a minor king, he manifests the body of a minor king and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who are to be saved by the form of an elder, he manifests the body of an elder and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be saved by means of the body of a lay devotee, he manifests the body of a lay devotee and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who should be saved by means of the body of a high official, he manifests the body of a high official and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who should be saved by means of the body of a Brahmin, he manifests the body of a Brahmin and preaches the Dharma for them.

To those who are to be delivered by means of the bodies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, he immediately manifests the bodies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who are to be delivered by means of the bodies of elders, lay devotees, officials, or Brahmin women, he immediately manifests the bodies of such women and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who are to be delivered by means of the bodies of young boys or young girls, he immediately manifests the bodies of young boys or young girls and preaches the Dharma for them.

To those who are to be delivered by means of the bodies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, or non-humans, he manifests all such forms and preaches the Dharma to them;
to those who are to be delivered by means of the body of a Vajrapāṇi, he manifests the body of a Vajrapāṇi and preaches the Dharma to them.
“Akṣayamati! This Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara has accomplished such meritorious virtues; appearing in various forms, he travels through all lands to deliver and liberate sentient beings.”
Therefore, you all should single-mindedly make offerings to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara is able to bestow fearlessness amidst terrors and urgent perils; for this reason, throughout this Sahā world, he is universally known as the "Bestower of Fearlessness."
The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall now make an offering to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.”
He immediately untied from his neck a multitude of precious jewels and necklaces, worth hundreds of thousands of taels of gold, and gave them to him, saying:
"O Benevolent One!"
"Please accept this precious necklace as a gift of Dharma.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva was unwilling to accept it.
Ajita further addressed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, saying:
“O Benevolent One!
Out of compassion for us, please accept this necklace.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara:

“Out of compassion for this Bodhisattva Akṣayamati and the fourfold assembly—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—please accept these necklaces.”

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for the fourfold assembly, as well as for the devas, nāgas, humans, and non-humans, accepted the necklace and divided it into two portions: one portion he offered to Śākyamuni Buddha, and the other portion he offered to the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
“Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such sovereign spiritual powers as these as he wanders through the Sahā world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati asked in verse:
“The World-Honored One, endowed with wondrous marks, I now ask you again:
For what cause and condition, O Son of the Buddha, is he named Avalokiteśvara?
To the one who possesses the complete and wondrous marks, the Honored One replied in verse to Akṣayamati:
"Listen to the practice of Avalokiteśvara, Who skillfully responds to all places and circumstances.
His great vows are as deep as the ocean, Spanning inconceivable eons.
Having attended many thousands of billions of Buddhas, He has made these vast and pure aspirations."
I shall briefly explain for you: hearing his name, seeing his body, or bringing him to mind—none of these pass in vain;
they can extinguish the suffering of all realms of existence.
Even if one were to harbor malice and push him down into a great pit of fire, [the merit would still prevail].
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, the fiery pit is transformed into a pool.
Or if drifting upon the vast ocean, amidst the perils of dragons, fish, and various spirits—
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, the waves cannot submerge them.
Or if one were on the peak of Mount Sumeru and pushed over by others, by virtue of the power of Avalokiteśvara, one would remain in the sky like the sun.
Or if pursued by evil men, one might fall onto the Diamond Mountains; yet by virtue of the power of Avalokiteśvara, one would remain in the sky like the sun.
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, not even a single hair can be harmed.
Or if one encounters hostile bandits surrounding them, each brandishing a blade to inflict injury,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they will all immediately give rise to a heart of compassion.
Or if one encounters the suffering of royal punishment, on the verge of execution when life is about to end,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, the blade is instantly shattered into pieces.
Or if one is imprisoned and shackled, with hands and feet bound by cangues and fetters,
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, one is released and attains liberation.
As for curses and various poisonous drugs intended to harm the body,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they return to the person who sent them.
Should one encounter evil rākṣasas, venomous dragons, various ghosts, and the like,
by recollecting the power of that Avalokiteśvara, they will all at once dare not cause harm.
Even if surrounded by fierce beasts with terrifying sharp fangs and claws, [one shall be safe].
By calling upon the power of Avalokiteśvara, one flees swiftly to boundless directions.
Even when vipers, snakes, and scorpions emit poisonous vapors like blazing fires,
by calling upon the power of Avalokiteśvara, they turn back of their own accord upon hearing the voice.
When clouds and thunder roll, lightning flashes, hail falls, and great rain pours down,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, these are dispersed and vanish in their time.
When sentient beings are beset by calamity and immeasurable suffering oppresses their bodies, [they find relief].
The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom Can rescue the world from suffering.
Possessing the power of supernormal faculties And extensively cultivating wisdom and skillful means,
Throughout the lands of the ten directions, There is no realm where he does not manifest his body.
The various evil destinies— hell, hungry ghosts, and animals—
and the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, are all gradually brought to extinction.
This is the true contemplation, the pure contemplation, the contemplation of vast wisdom.
Contemplating compassion and contemplating loving-kindness, may I always aspire to and gaze upon you.
With stainless, pure radiance, the sun of wisdom shatters all darkness;
it can subdue the winds and fires of calamity, shining universally upon the world.
The thunderous roar of the precepts, whose essence is compassion, and the wondrous great cloud of a benevolent mind,
pour down the nectar-rain of the Dharma, extinguishing the flames of affliction.
Whether in legal disputes before government officials or amidst the terrors of battle arrays, [this rain provides relief].
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, all enemies shall retreat and disperse.
With his wondrous voice, his voice that observes the world, his Brahma-voice, and his ocean-tide voice—
surpassing all sounds in the world— one should therefore always keep him in mind.
Do not give rise to doubt at any thought.
Amidst the perils of suffering and death, he is able to act as a refuge;
endowed with all virtues, he gazes upon sentient beings with eyes of compassion.
"The ocean of merit is immeasurable; therefore, one should pay homage with the crown of the head.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and said to him:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are sentient beings who hear this chapter on the Sovereign Acts of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the supernatural powers manifested through the Universal Gate, you should know that the merit of such persons is not small.

When the Buddha spoke this "Universal Gate" Chapter, eighty-four thousand sentient beings within the assembly all resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, which is peerless.

Chapter 26: Dharani. The Lotus Sutra, Chapter Twenty-Six: Dharani. At that time, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are good sons or good daughters who are able to receive and uphold the Lotus Sūtra—whether by reading and reciting it until they have mastered it, or by copying its scrolls—how much merit will they obtain?
The Buddha told Bhaiṣajyarāja:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who make offerings to as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in eight hundred million nayutas of Ganges Rivers."
"What do you think?
Is the merit obtained thereby not great?
"It is very great, World-Honored One."
The Buddha said:

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family is able, regarding this sutra, to even receive and uphold a single four-line verse, reciting it, explaining its meaning, and practicing according to the teaching, their merit will be exceedingly great."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall now bestow upon the teacher of the Dharma a dhāraṇī mantra to protect them.”
He then spoke the mantra,
saying: "An-e (1) Man-e (2)"
Mame samama me ji le.
Cchili (6) śame (7) śarigade (8) svāhā.

jiumuti, mudi, muli. 11.

The first is named Many-Haired; the second, No-Satiety; the third, Holder-of-Necklaces; the fourth, Gaudī; the fifth, Seizer-of-the-Essence-and-Vitality-of-all-Sentient-Beings. “World-Honored One!”
We, too, desire to protect those who read, recite, receive, and uphold the Lotus Sutra, removing their misfortunes and afflictions.
If there should be anyone who seeks out the faults of the Dharma Master, we shall ensure they find no opportunity.
Thereupon, before the Buddha, he spoke this incantation:

He then spoke these verses before the Buddha:
“If anyone does not comply with my spell And disturbs the one who preaches the Dharma,

As is the crime of killing one's parents, as is the calamity of crushing oil,

When the rākṣasīs had spoken these verses, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
