The Buddha addressed the rākṣasīs:
“Excellent, excellent!

If you can merely protect those who receive and uphold the name of the Lotus Sutra, their merit will be immeasurable; how much more so for those whom you protect who fully receive and uphold it, making offerings to the sutra scrolls with flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, ointment incense, burning incense, banners, canopies, and music?”
They lit various kinds of lamps:

lamps of ghee, lamps of oil, lamps of various fragrant oils, lamps of *sumana* flower oil, lamps of *campaka* flower oil, lamps of *vārṣika* flower oil, and lamps of *utpala* flower oil—making hundreds of thousands of such offerings.
"Kauṣṭhila!
You and your retinue should protect such Dharma-preachers as these.
When this "Chapter on the Dhāraṇī" was spoken, sixty-eight thousand people attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Past Deeds of King Subhavyūha At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly:

"In the distant past, beyond immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Meghadundubhisvararājasaṃkusumitābhijña, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. His land was named Prabhāvyūha, and his eon was named Priyadarśana."

In that Buddha-dharma, there was a king named Wondrous Adornment (Sudarśana); the king’s queen was named Pure Virtue (Viśuddhaguṇā), and they had two sons: the first was named Pure Treasury (Viśuddhagarbha), and the second was named Pure Eye (Viśuddhanetra).

These two sons possess great supernormal powers, merit, and wisdom; they have long cultivated the path practiced by bodhisattvas—namely, the dāna-pāramitā, śīla-pāramitā, kṣānti-pāramitā, vīrya-pāramitā, dhyāna-pāramitā, prajñā-pāramitā, and upāya-pāramitā—as well as loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, and even the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, all of which they have clearly understood and thoroughly mastered.

Furthermore, he attained the Bodhisattva’s Pure Samādhi, the Sun and Stars Samādhi, the Pure Light Samādhi, the Pure Color Samādhi, the Pure Illumination Samādhi, the Long Adornment Samādhi, and the Great Majestic Virtue Treasury Samādhi; he also fully mastered and penetrated all these samādhis.
At that time, that Buddha, wishing to guide King Subhavyūha and out of compassion for sentient beings, preached this Lotus Sutra.
Then the two sons, Viśuddhagarbha and Viśuddhanetra, went to their mother’s place and, joining their ten fingers in palms-together salutation, said:
“We pray that you, Mother, will go to the presence of the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararājapuṣpadhvaja-jñāna; we too shall serve as attendants, drawing near to him, making offerings, and prostrating.”
"Why is this? This Buddha is preaching the Lotus Sūtra amidst the assembly of all devas and humans; you ought to listen to and receive it.
The mother said to her son:
"Your father has faith in and accepts the teachings of external paths; he is deeply attached to the Brahmanical dharma. You should go and inform your father so that you may go together with him.
Pure Treasury and Pure Eye joined their palms with ten fingers interlaced and said to their mother:
"We are sons of the Dharma King, yet we have been born into this family of false views."
The mother said to her sons:
"You should take concern for your father and manifest supernatural transformations for him; if he should see them, his mind will surely become pure, or he may permit us to go to where the Buddha is."

Thereupon, out of filial concern for their father, the two sons leaped into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and manifested various supernatural transformations: they walked, stood, sat, and lay down in mid-air;
water issued from the upper part of their bodies while fire issued from the lower, and fire issued from the lower part of their bodies while water issued from the upper;
they manifested massive bodies that filled the void and then became small again, or became small and then large again.
He vanished from mid-air and suddenly appeared upon the ground;
he entered the earth as if it were water and walked upon the water as if it were solid ground.
Manifesting such various supernatural transformations, he caused his father, the King, to attain pure faith and understanding.

At that time, seeing his sons’ supernatural powers to be such as these, the father was filled with great joy at having attained what he had never experienced before; joining his palms toward his sons, he said:
"Who is your teacher, and whose disciples are you?"
The two sons addressed him, saying:
"Great King!

That Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom is currently seated upon the Dharma-throne beneath the Bodhi tree made of the seven precious substances, extensively preaching the Lotus Sūtra amidst the assembly of devas and humans of all worlds. He is our teacher; we are his disciples."
The father said to his sons, "I now also wish to see your teacher; let us go together.
Thereupon, the two sons descended from the sky to where their mother was, and with palms joined, they addressed her:
"Father the King has now attained faith and understanding and is capable of resolving his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
We have already performed the work of a Buddha for our father; we pray that you, Mother, will grant us leave to go forth from home and practice the Way under that Buddha."
At that time, the two sons, wishing to restate their intention, addressed their mother in verse:
“May our mother release us, so that we may leave the home life and become śramaṇas.
Buddhas are extremely difficult to encounter; we shall follow the Buddha and train.”
“As rare as the udumbara flower, it is even more difficult to encounter a Buddha;
it is likewise difficult to escape from all calamities. I pray that you will grant me permission to leave the home life.
Her mother then said to her:
"I grant you permission to go forth.
Why is this? Because a Buddha is difficult to encounter."
Then the two sons said to their parents:
"Excellent, parents!
We pray that you will go at once to the place where the Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Abiding-King-Flower-Wisdom resides, to attend upon him and make offerings."
Why is this? A Buddha is difficult to encounter, like the udumbara flower, or like a one-eyed turtle encountering the hole in a floating log.

Yet we, through the profound depth of our past merit, have been born to encounter the Buddha-dharma; therefore, parents, you should grant us permission to leave the household life and become renunciants.
"Why is this? Because Buddhas are difficult to encounter, and such times are also difficult to meet.
At that time, the eighty-four thousand women in King Subhavyūha’s inner palace were all capable of receiving and upholding this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
The Bodhisattva Viśuddhanetra has long since attained mastery in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*;

the Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha has, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, attained mastery in the *Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-samādhi*, desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave behind all evil destinies.
The king’s consort had attained the Samādhi of the Gathering of All Buddhas and was able to know the secret treasury of all Buddhas.
"In this way, the two sons used the power of skillful means to skillfully transform their father, causing his mind to attain faith and understanding, and to take delight in the Buddha-dharma."

Thereupon, King Wonderful Adornment, together with his ministers and retinue; Lady Pure Virtue, together with the ladies of the inner palace and her attendants; and the king’s two sons, together with forty-two thousand people, all went at once to the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the Buddha preached the Dharma for the king, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him.
The King was filled with great joy.

At that time, King Subhavyūha and his queen took off necklaces of genuine pearls worth hundreds of thousands from their necks and scattered them over the Buddha. In mid-air, these transformed into a precious four-pillared pavilion. Within the pavilion was a great jeweled couch spread with hundreds of thousands of millions of celestial robes. Upon it sat the Buddha in the full lotus posture, emitting a great radiance.
At that time, King Subhavyūha had this thought:
"The Buddha’s body is rare and marvelous; it is upright, dignified, and extraordinary, having perfected the foremost and most subtle of forms."
Then the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararāja-pūrvapraṇidhānaguṇasamudgata addressed the fourfold assembly, saying:
"Do you see this King Subhavyūha standing before me with his palms joined?"

This king shall become a bhikṣu within my Dharma; through diligent cultivation and assistance to the Buddha’s path, he shall attain Buddhahood, named Śālarājā, with a land called Mahāprabha and an eon called Mahocchrayarāja.
"That King of Śāla Trees Buddha has an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas and an immeasurable number of śrāvakas; his land is level and upright, and its merits are such as these.

Thereupon, the king immediately entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother and, together with his consort, two sons, and all his retinue, left the household life to practice the Way within the Buddha-dharma.
“After the king had renounced the world, for eighty-four thousand years he constantly practiced with diligent vigor, cultivating the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.

Following this period, he attained the *Sarva-viśuddha-guṇa-vyūha-samādhi* (the Samādhi Adorned with All Pure Merits). He then ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!...’”

"These two sons of mine have already performed the work of a Buddha; by means of their supernatural transformations, they have turned back my perverse mind, causing me to dwell securely within the Buddha-dharma and enabling me to behold the World-Honored One."
"These two sons are my spiritual friends; wishing to arouse the roots of goodness from my past lives and to bring me benefit, they have been born into my family."
At that time, the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararāja-pūrvayugaśrīguṇasāgarabuddhi addressed King Suśobhita, saying:
"So it is, so it is! It is just as you have said."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, by virtue of having planted roots of goodness, obtains virtuous friends in every lifetime; those virtuous friends are able to perform the work of a Buddha, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them, causing them to enter into anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Great King!

You should know that a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) is a great causal condition; that is to say, they transform and guide others so that they may behold the Buddha and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Great King!
Do you see these two sons?

These two sons have already made offerings to sixty-five hundred thousand million billion nayutas of Ganges-sands of Buddhas, attending and revering them. Under those Buddhas, they upheld the Lotus Sutra and, out of compassion for sentient beings with wrong views, caused them to abide in right view."
King Wonderful Adornment immediately descended from mid-air and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One! The Tathāgata is most rare and extraordinary;

by virtue of his merit and wisdom, the light from the *uṣṇīṣa* on the crown of his head shines forth brilliantly. His eyes are long and wide, a deep azure-blue; the tuft of hair between his eyebrows is white as a conch or the moon; his teeth are white, even, and closely set, constantly emitting radiance; and the color of his lips is beautiful and red, like the *bimba* fruit."

At that time, King Wonderful Adornment, having praised the Buddha for such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of merits, joined his palms with single-minded devotion before the Tathāgata and addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
It is truly marvelous!
The Dharma of the Tathāgata is fully endowed with inconceivable and subtle merits; its instructions for practice bring peace, security, and sublime well-being.
"From this day forward, I shall no longer act according to my own whims; I shall not give rise to wrong views, arrogance, malice, or any other evil thoughts.
Having spoken these words, he prostrated before the Buddha and departed.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly:
"What do you think?
Is King Wonderful Adornment anyone other than this person?"
The Bodhisattva Flower Virtue (Huade) is this very person.
As for Lady Pure Virtue (Jingde), she is the Bodhisattva Radiant Adorned Appearance (Guangzao Zhuangyanxiang) now before the Buddha.
Out of compassion for King Wondrous Adornment (Miaozhuangyan) and his retinue, she was born there.
Those two sons are none other than the present Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja and the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.

These Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata have accomplished such great merits as these; they have planted the roots of all virtues under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas and have perfected inconceivable wholesome merits.
"If there are those who know the names of these two bodhisattvas, all the devas and people of the world should also pay them homage.

When the Buddha preached this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of King Subhavyūha," eighty-four thousand people were distanced from and freed of dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.

Chapter Twenty-Eight: Encouragement by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, by means of his sovereign supernatural powers, majestic virtue, and renown, arrived from the east accompanied by an immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable number of great bodhisattvas.
All the lands through which he passed trembled universally; precious lotus flowers rained down, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of various kinds of music were played.

Surrounded by a great assembly of countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, each manifesting their majestic power and supernatural faculties, he arrived at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the Sahā world. There, he prostrated with his head at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and addressed the Buddha, saying:

“World-Honored One, from the land of the Buddha Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja, I have heard from afar that the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* is being preached in this Sahā world. Together with immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of bodhisattvas, I have come to hear and receive it; I only pray that the World-Honored One will preach it for us.”
“If good sons or good daughters, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, wish to obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, how can they do so?
The Buddha told Samantabhadra Bodhisattva:
“If good sons or good daughters accomplish four dharmas, they shall obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata.”

First, they are protected and remembered by all Buddhas; second, they plant the roots of all virtues; third, they enter the stage of right determination; fourth, they give rise to the mind that seeks to save all sentient beings.
“Good sons and good daughters, those who thus accomplish these four dharmas will, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, certainly obtain this sutra.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

In the final five hundred years, during the age of turbidity and evil, should there be those who receive, uphold, and recite this sutra, I shall protect them, eliminate their misfortunes and afflictions, and cause them to attain peace and security. I shall ensure that no one seeking to find an opportunity against them can succeed—neither Māras, nor the sons of Māra, nor the daughters of Māra, nor the followers of Māra, nor those possessed by Māra; neither yakṣas, nor rākṣasas, nor kumbhāṇḍas, nor piśācas, nor kiṃnaras, nor pūtanas, nor vetālas, or any other beings who torment humans—all such as these shall find no opportunity to harm them.

If this person, whether walking or standing, reads and recites this sutra, at that time I shall mount the white elephant king with six tusks and, together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas, go to their location, manifesting my own body to provide offerings and protection, and to comfort their minds; this is also for the sake of making offerings to the Lotus Sutra.

If this person sits and contemplates this sutra, at that time I shall again mount the king of white elephants and manifest before that person. If there be even a single phrase or a single verse of the Lotus Sutra that they have forgotten, I shall instruct them, recite it with them, and cause them to master it once more.

At that time, those who receive, uphold, read, and recite the Lotus Sutra shall behold my body; they will experience immense joy and become even more diligent. Because they have seen me, they will immediately attain samādhis and dhāraṇīs, namely the *Svayambhū-dhāraṇī*, the *Koṭīśatasahasrasvayambhū-dhāraṇī*, and the *Dharmaghoṣopāya-dhāraṇī*. They shall attain such dhāraṇīs as these.
“World-Honored One!

If, in a future age, during the final five hundred years of a turbid and evil world, there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who seek, uphold, recite, or transcribe this Lotus Sūtra, and desire to practice it, they should, for a period of twenty-one days, apply themselves with single-minded diligence.”

When the twenty-one days have passed, I shall mount a six-tusked white elephant, surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas, and manifest before that person with a body that all sentient beings delight to behold, preaching the Dharma for them, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening them. I shall also bestow upon them this dhāraṇī mantra; because they obtain this dhāraṇī, no non-human being shall be able to destroy them, nor shall they be deluded or disturbed by women, and I myself shall also constantly protect such a person.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will permit me to recite this dhāraṇī mantra.
He then spoke the mantra before the Buddha, saying:

“*Atandī* (1), *tandāpade* (2), *tandāpade* (3), *tandākūśale* (4), *tandāsudale* (5), *sudale* (6), *sudharapate* (7), *niḥ* (8), *saṃghanirghātani* (9), *asaṃkhye* (10), *saṃgapagati* (11), *trela-dro-saṃga-tau-lak-āra-te-vara-te* (12), *sarvasaṃgasamādhi-garande* (13), *sarvadharmasuparikṣite* (14), *sarvasattvaraudrakṣayānugate* (15), *khambigilantide* (16). “World-Honored One!...”

If there are bodhisattvas who hear this dhāraṇī, they should know it is the power of Samantabhadra’s spiritual transformations. If the Lotus Sūtra circulates in Jambudvīpa and there are those who receive and uphold it, they should form this thought:
"All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra."

"If there are those who receive and uphold, read and recite, correctly contemplate, understand the meaning and intent of this, and practice according to what is taught, you should know that such persons perform the conduct of Samantabhadra; they have deeply planted roots of goodness in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, and their heads are stroked by the hands of all Tathāgatas."

If one merely copies it down, at the end of that person's life, they shall be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; at that time, eighty-four thousand celestial maidens will come to welcome them with various musical performances, and the person will immediately don a crown of the seven treasures and enjoy themselves in pleasure among the court ladies.
How much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, understand its meaning and intent, and practice according to the teaching!

If there are those who receive and uphold, read and recite, and understand the meaning and intent of this, at the end of their lives, these people will be reached by the hands of a thousand Buddhas, who will cause them to have no fear and not fall into the evil realms, but instead go directly to the presence of Maitreya Bodhisattva in the Tuṣita Heaven above.

Maitreya Bodhisattva, surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas endowed with the thirty-two marks, together with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of celestial maidens as his retinue, will be born therein; such are the merits and benefits thereof.

Therefore, the wise person should with single-minded devotion either write it themselves or have others write it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, maintain right mindfulness of it, and practice according to its teaching.
“World-Honored One!
By means of my supernormal powers, I shall now protect this sutra and cause it to be widely circulated within Jambudvīpa after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, so that it shall not be interrupted.”
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent,
Samantabhadra!"
"You are able to protect and assist this sutra, bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to many sentient beings.

You have already accomplished inconceivable merit and possess profound, great compassion; having long ago resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you are able to make such a vow of supernatural power to guard and protect this sutra."
"I shall, by means of my supernormal powers, protect those who are able to receive and uphold the name of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Samantabhadra!

If there are those who receive and uphold, read and recite, correctly recollect, cultivate, and transcribe this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, you should know that such persons see Śākyamuni Buddha, as if hearing this sūtra directly from the Buddha’s own mouth."
One should know that this person has made offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha;
one should know that this person is praised by the Buddha as "Excellent!";
one should know that this person has had his head stroked by the hand of Śākyamuni Buddha.
You should know that such a person is covered by the robe of Śākyamuni Buddha.

Such a person no longer craves worldly pleasures; they do not take delight in the scriptures or the writings of non-Buddhists, nor do they enjoy associating with those people or various evildoers—whether they be butchers, or those who raise pigs, sheep, chickens, or dogs, or hunters, or those who trade in female beauty.
This person’s mind is upright and honest; they possess right mindfulness and the power of merit.
Such a person is not afflicted by the three poisons, nor are they afflicted by envy, self-conceit, false pride, or overweening pride;
such a person has few desires and is content, and is able to cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra.
“Samantabhadra!
If, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, during the final five hundred years, there should be anyone who sees another receiving, upholding, reading, or reciting the Lotus Sūtra, they should think:

‘This person shall before long proceed to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), destroy the hosts of Māras, attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, turn the wheel of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma; they shall sit upon the lion Dharma-seat amidst the great assembly of devas and humans.’”
“Samantabhadra!

If, in future ages, there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, such persons shall no longer be greedily attached to clothing, bedding, food and drink, or the necessities of life; their aspirations shall not be in vain, and they shall also obtain their karmic rewards in this present life.”
If someone should despise and revile them, saying:
"You are merely a madman; practicing such deeds in vain, you shall ultimately gain nothing," as a retribution for such a sin, they shall be born blind life after life.
If there are those who make offerings to or praise [this person], they shall obtain visible retribution in this very life.
Furthermore, if anyone sees one who upholds this sutra and exposes their faults—whether those faults be real or unreal—that person shall suffer from leprosy in this present life.

If there are those who mock or deride [this teaching], they shall, in every lifetime, have teeth that are sparse and missing, ugly lips, flat noses, contorted hands and feet, squinting eyes, and bodies foul with stench; they shall suffer from malignant sores, pus and blood, dropsy, shortness of breath, and various other grave and evil illnesses.
"Therefore, Samantabhadra!
If you see one who receives and upholds this sutra, you should go out to welcome them from afar, as if paying respect to the Buddha.

When this "Chapter on Samantabhadra’s Exhortation" was spoken, immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, attained hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *dhāraṇīs* of revolving.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within a trichiliocosm, who had perfected the path of Samantabhadra, were present.

When the Buddha preached this sutra, the entire great assembly—including Samantabhadra and the other bodhisattvas, Śāriputra and the other śrāvakas, as well as devas, nāgas, humans, non-humans, and others—were all filled with great joy. They received and upheld the Buddha’s words, paid their respects, and departed.

The Postscript to the Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Scroll Seven. Composed by the Śramaṇa Sengrui of the Later Qin. The *Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma* is the secret treasury of all Buddhas and the essential reality of all scriptures.
To name it after the "Huá" (Lotus) is to illuminate its essence;
to call it "Fénduólì" (Puṇḍarīka) is to praise its magnificence.
Since that which is aroused is profound and its purport is exceedingly subtle, were it not for those of penetrating insight to transmit it, few would find the gateway to it.
Now, the hundred species of medicinal herbs are the essence of plants and the foundation of all things;
the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dharma are the source of the fruits of the Path. Therefore, they are used as a metaphor.
Among all flowers, the lotus is the most excellent. When the flower has not yet opened, it is called *kumuda*;
when it has opened and is about to fall, it is called *kamala*;
and when it is in its full bloom, it is called *puṇḍarīka*.

The unopened flower serves as a metaphor for the two paths; the imminent falling of petals is likened to Nirvana; and its radiant splendor alone is sufficient to serve as a metaphor for this scripture.
As for the various *Prajñā* sūtras, there is no depth they do not exhaust, and thus seekers of the Way return by means of them;
there is no greatness they do not encompass, and thus those who ride the vehicle are delivered by means of them.
However, its general outline takes "adapting to transformation" as paramount;
regarding the gateway of responding to affairs, it cannot but employ "skillful means" (upāya).

As for the transformative power of skillful means, although its awakening of beings is vast, it is insufficient for the ultimate reality; that this belongs to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* is indeed fitting.

Upon investigating its profound purport, one finds it vast, expansive, and deep; its scope extends exceedingly far. How could it merely consist of explaining reality, returning to the fundamental, and definitively resolving divergent paths?
This is indeed the Great, Luminous Principle of Awakening, encompassing all from antiquity to the present.
It is said that the Buddha’s lifespan is immeasurable; even eternal kalpas are insufficient to clarify its duration.
His manifested bodies are innumerable; even ten thousand forms are insufficient to differentiate his essence.

Thus, the span of his life is fixed as being beyond calculation; his manifested bodies clarify that he has no substantial reality; Samantabhadra reveals that he has no attainment; and Prabhūtaratna illuminates that he is subject to no extinction.
If one traverses from the profound antiquity to the present day, then ten thousand generations are but a single day;
if one contemplates the myriad transformations to awaken to the profound mystery, then a thousand paths share no different tracks.
Being thus, the process of birth and life is not sufficient to be termed "existence," and eternal stillness likewise cannot be said to be "extinction."
If one seeks the profound essence to sever the past, one loses all achievement in primordial non-being;
if one restrains the reins of the mind within samādhi, one forgets all expectations regarding the two stages.
Although this scripture has circulated in this land for nearly a century, the translators were ignorant of its empty ford, and the numinous gate remained unopened.
Discourssants have deviated from its standard principles, and its profound traces are rarely trodden;
in vain do they search and study until their hair turns white, yet none has even caught a glimpse of its gateway.

Yao Song, the Commandant of the Imperial Secretariat of Qin, General of the Left, and Marquis of Ancheng, aligns his rhythm with the Mysterious Gate and dwells his mind beyond the mundane world. He pours forth his sincerity into this scripture, his faith reaching its utmost limit. Whenever he contemplates its text, he deeply perceives the errors of the translators.

Having encountered Dharma Master Kumārajīva, he had him transcribe it; its ultimate truth was revealed as clearly as if one were piercing through the heavy clouds to soar aloft, or ascending Mount Kunlun to look down with a sweeping gaze.

At that time, there were over eight hundred monks who listened to, received, and understood [the teachings]; they were all the most eminent and outstanding talents from every quarter, the paragons of their era.
This was the eighth year of Hongshi, when the celestial stem and branch cycle reached Chunchu (the Fire-Hare year).

On this occasion of the distant anniversary of the passing of her late husband, the Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister Li Gong, Lady Zhang of the State of Lu respectfully bestows one thousand coins as pure wealth upon the Office of the Tripitaka at Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou. She commissions the carving of seven fascicles of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* (The Lotus Sutra) and three fascicles of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi-sūtra* and other scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, inscribed with phoenix-patterned characters. By virtue of these meritorious causes, she prays that her husband may ascend to the Pure Land and be honored therein.
Respectfully inscribed on the fifteenth day of the first month in the twenty-first year of the Shaoxing era. Attached: Imperial Preface to the *Avalokiteśvara Pumenpin Sūtra*.

The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, with a *śakrābhilagna* (indestructible) mind, manifests infinite transformations; through sovereign spiritual powers (*ṛddhi*), he wanders throughout the entire Dharma-realm. He enters lands as numerous as motes of dust to preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings. Possessing wondrous marks and vows as vast as the ocean, whenever there is a karmic affinity and one gives rise to a pure heart, the moment a voice is raised in invocation, he responds according to that sound, and all desires and aspirations are immediately fulfilled as wished.
The "Universal Gate Chapter" of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* is the true exposition for the liberation from suffering and affliction.

If a person can constantly cultivate contemplation based on this sūtra, then at the very moment a single thought arises, they will immediately behold the supreme form of Great Compassion, which is able to extinguish all forms of suffering; its merit is inconceivable.

I, the Emperor, reflect that the Way of Heaven bestows blessings upon the virtuous and brings calamity upon the licentious; thus the Buddha reveals the retribution of karmic fruits to lead people toward goodness and deter them from evil.

Indeed, both heaven and hell are created by human beings themselves and do not exist apart from within one's own mind; therefore, those who perform good deeds ascend to heaven, while those who commit evil fall into hell.

Indeed, for loyal ministers, filial sons, auspicious persons, and upright scholars, their very minds are the Buddha; therefore, they are protected and aided by the divine spirits, and their karmic obstructions are entirely extinguished. Consequently, while alive they do not violate the laws, and after death they do not fall into the Avīci Hell.

As for those who are cruel and obstinate, they are single-mindedly devoted to evil; they cast aside the five human relations as if they were worn-out brooms, and they tread upon laws and punishments as if drinking something sweet. They would rather feed themselves to a rākṣasa than revere the Buddha-dharma.
However, human nature is fundamentally good; those who act wickedly do so merely due to the partiality of their innate dispositions (*qi-zhi*).
If one can reform the heart and change one's thoughts, practicing self-examination and exercising caution, then through such a transformation, evil can be turned into goodness.

If one performs good, one immediately becomes a virtuous person; the faults accumulated in the past will vanish completely—like a speck of dust in the vast void or a flake of snow in a red-hot furnace—and even if there were karmic retribution, where could it be applied?

I have constantly reflected upon this, fearing only that people of the world might commit transgressions and fail to know how to reform them, thereby willingly abandoning themselves. Consequently, I have had this scripture edited and published, so that virtuous gentlemen may forever strengthen their resolve toward self-restraint, embrace immeasurable blessings, and cultivate goodness; how could such meritorious virtue ever have a limit?

The measure of power, the measure of majestic virtue, the measure of the locus of meaning, the Moon-Lamp Radiant Mark, the Ocean of All Marks, the Sovereign King of Wisdom and Mastery over Supernormal Powers, the Foot with Marks of Ten Million Rays, the Joy of Tranquility, and the Wisdom of Those Who Fear.
